narration: That hundred-and-thirty-dollar quote looks cheaper. But it leaves out the part we actually need. Until someone prices the seal, we don't know the bill.
You can open the quote and check that yourself. The other one is a hundred and forty-five dollars, with the standard seal included.
Say our limit is a hundred and forty dollars. The assistant stops here. It doesn't call an unknown bill affordable. I'll change that limit to a hundred and fifty, explicitly.
Homekind, Monday afternoon, with Sam at home. The app checked the scope and both calendars. Sam reviews the details and approves. So far, a perfectly ordinary plan.
Then Sam's schedule changes. This is the bit I care about. That Monday plan is withdrawn immediately. A yes for an old plan must never become a yes for a different one.
Find another time. Tuesday works for Alex, and the price is still a hundred and forty-five dollars. Same repair, same budget. A new plan, with a new approval request.
Alex checks the details and confirms. Reload the page: the decision and the change history are still here. Nobody has contacted a contractor or charged a card.

This is a working MCP service, with planning and calendar changes called over real HTTP from the web app. The household and quotes are simulated. When life changes, yesterday's permission isn't enough.
